en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, found in Mindanao, has a distinctive crest of long brown feathers.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater lake located inside a large volcanic caldera.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Philippines is a top global producer of abaca, a banana plant species whose fibers make strong ropes.
The Philippine Sea, located east of the archipelago, contains the Philippine Trench, one of the deepest ocean trenches globally.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon season in the Philippines that typically brings dry weather from November to April.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, is one of the smallest primates and has enormous eyes for night vision.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Benguet province in the Cordillera Administrative Region is called the Salad Bowl of the Philippines due to its vegetable production.
